# Thesis: a late-day liquidity-reversal signal blended with three slow signals (R&D intensity, net issuance, low accruals), size-neutral, traded once a week. Accrual returns move AGAINST short-term reversal returns (daily PnL corr -.2 in our tests), so the blend keeps reversal IR with less turnover and less overlap with crowded reversal alphas.
# Source: liquidity reversal (Campbell, Grossman & Wang, QJE 1993); R&D intensity (Chan, Lakonishok & Sougiannis, JF 2001); net share issuance (Pontiff & Woodgate, JF 2008); accruals (Sloan, The Accounting Review 1996, https://www.jstor.org/stable/248290)
# Repair: accruals weight 1.5x (accruals added IR when swapped in, so more of it should cut turnover without the IR loss gross profit caused). Parent R_RIAwk (portal #705948) IR .080, TVR .248, irtvr .161, corr .573 to #601796 (bar .169: needs TVR <= .224 at the same IR, or corr < .5).
g = ts_mean((close - vwap_last_hour)/vwap_last_hour, 5)  # 5-day avg close-vs-VWAP gap
busy = cs_rank(number_of_trades_last_hour/ts_mean(number_of_trades_last_hour, 20)) > 1.3  # unusually many last-hour trades
r = cs_zscore(at_zero2nan(-cs_rank(g) * busy))  # fade the gap on busy closes
k1 = cs_zscore(cs_rank(ts_fill(research_and_development_expense)/mktcap))  # R&D intensity per dollar of market value
k2 = cs_zscore(-cs_rank(shsout/ts_delay(shsout, 250) - 1))  # net issuance: short dilution, long buybacks
k3 = cs_zscore(-cs_rank((ts_fill(net_income) - ts_fill(cash_from_operations))/ts_fill(total_assets)))  # low accruals: earnings backed by cash
sz = cs_rank(at_signlog(mktcap))  # size rank (log market cap)
s = at_nan2zero(cs_factorneut(at_zero2nan(at_nan2zero(r) + at_nan2zero(k1) + at_nan2zero(k2) + 1.5*at_nan2zero(k3)), [sz]))  # blend with accruals at 1.5x, size neutral
f0 = (day_of_the_week*0 + 1)*(day_of_the_week < ts_delay(day_of_the_week, 1))  # 1.0 on the first trading day of the week (float32)
f1 = ts_delay(f0, 1)  # week started yesterday
f2 = ts_delay(f0, 2)  # week started 2 days ago
f3 = ts_delay(f0, 3)  # week started 3 days ago
alpha = at_zero2nan(f0*s + (1-f0)*(f1*ts_delay(s, 1) + (1-f1)*(f2*ts_delay(s, 2) + (1-f2)*(f3*ts_delay(s, 3) + (1-f3)*ts_delay(s, 4)))))  # hold the week-start book all week

# Thesis: fade late-day price pressure (VWAP gap on busy closes plus heavy-volume last-hour moves), size/vol neutral, blended with LOW ACCRUALS. Accrual returns move against short-term reversal returns, so the blend keeps reversal IR with less turnover and less overlap with crowded reversal alphas.
# Source: liquidity reversal (Campbell, Grossman & Wang, QJE 1993); accruals (Sloan, The Accounting Review 1996, https://www.jstor.org/stable/248290)
# Repair: accrual weight 1.2 -> 1.6 to cut turnover. Parent Y_PLsz_ACC_w12 IR .116, TVR .711, irtvr .138, corr .979 to our #698181 (bar .144; needs TVR <= .649).
g = ts_mean((close - vwap_last_hour)/vwap_last_hour, 5)  # 5-day avg close-vs-VWAP gap
busy = cs_rank(number_of_trades_last_hour/ts_mean(number_of_trades_last_hour, 20)) > 1.3  # unusually many last-hour trades
p1 = cs_zscore(at_zero2nan(-cs_rank(g) * busy))  # fade the gap on busy closes
a1 = cs_rank(ts_mean(return_last_hour, 5))  # 5-day avg last-hour return rank
hot = cs_rank(volume/ts_mean(volume, 20)) > 1.3  # unusually heavy volume
p2 = cs_zscore(at_zero2nan(-(a1 + cs_rank(g)) * hot))  # fade late-day moves on heavy volume
sz = cs_rank(at_signlog(mktcap))  # size rank
vo = cs_rank(ts_std(ret1, 20))  # 1-month volatility rank
rev = cs_zscore(cs_factorneut(at_zero2nan(at_nan2zero(p1) + at_nan2zero(p2)), [sz, vo]))  # size/vol-neutral reversal
k = cs_zscore(-cs_rank((ts_fill(net_income) - ts_fill(cash_from_operations))/ts_fill(total_assets)))  # low accruals: earnings backed by cash
alpha = at_zero2nan(at_nan2zero(rev) + 1.6*at_nan2zero(k))  # reversal + 1.6x accruals
